A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 10-page versions of the same work, with corresponding sections, equations, figures, and tables. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original FFHQ evaluations, qualitative ablations, stylized face-swapping results, and a 39-participant human evaluation in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains the work's original quantitative results, qualitative experiments, and human evaluation, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 6–9.

M1.justification: V1 Section 3.2 describes an additional InsightFace 3D-pose estimate encoded with Fourier features and concatenated to the fused conditioning. V2 deletes this paragraph, while retaining the other architecture descriptions, equations, and training stages. The PDFs do not establish whether the component was removed from the method or only from its documentation.

E1.justification: Both retain the 4.5-million-image identity-paired training collection, filtered LAION-5B faces for post-training, FFHQ evaluation, and stylized targets. No dataset, task, or domain coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 6 and Table 1 retain SimSwap, E4S, InfoSwap, DiffFace, DiffSwap, and REFace. Table 2 also retains the same listed comparison methods. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Reported settings remain Stable Diffusion 1.5, 1,000 FFHQ validation pairs, 512 × 512 outputs, the same evaluation metrics, and 39 human participants. The equal-training-volume control for non-decoupled conditioning is also unchanged.

E4.justification: The decoupled-conditioning comparison in Figure 8, training-stage analysis in Figure 9, and stylized-target robustness examples in Figures 1 and 7 are retained without new or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 are unchanged, including the proposed method's FID of 3.61, Top-1 identity retrieval of 97.90, and fidelity preference of 57.1%. The qualitative figure images and reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the diffusion formulation, conditioning equations, and loss descriptions remain unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about decoupled condition injection, identity-constrained multi-stage training, and state-of-the-art face swapping. The shortened conclusion preserves these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning identity–attribute competition, refinement losses, stylized-image generalization, lighting, and face-shape adjustment remain unchanged. A deleted concluding sentence repeats the retained prospect of applying the approach to broader conditional generation.

D1.justification: V2 removes the named pose-estimation tool, Fourier-embedding recipe, concatenation instruction, and associated InsightFace reference/link from Section 3.2. This is a definite reduction in documented technical information; the remaining implementation and training disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds four references concerning noisy-face representations, LLM prompt encoding, masked-face recognition, and EasyRef, and removes the InsightFace entry. These are limited citation changes; the related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 corrects 'source fave' to 'source face', updates affiliations and contact information, adds acknowledgements, and trims the conclusion. The section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 moves from page 6 to page 5, Figure 6 shifts upward, Figures 7–8 are slightly enlarged, and Tables 1–2 are reduced in size. All nine figures and both tables retain their content.

improvement.justification: V2 makes small editorial and layout updates while retaining identical empirical evidence. However, deleting the explicit pose-conditioning recipe could correct an obsolete description or omit needed reproducibility information; the PDFs do not resolve which. This prevents a reliable judgment of the net effect on paper quality.
